environment.description: Same Lambda function deployed in a hardened account. The Lambda is placed inside a VPC with private subnets only (no NAT gateway for metadata). Egress is routed through a transparent forward proxy (Squid 4.x on EC2) that maintains a domain allowlist. However, the PRIMARY control is a VPC endpoint policy on the execute-api VPC endpoint that restricts invocation sources, combined with the fact that Lambda functions in VPC cannot reach 169.254.169.254 (IMDS) because VPC-attached Lambdas use a Firecracker microVM network namespace where the metadata service credential vending is handled via internal Lambda runtime API (169.254.100.2) rather than IMDS. The Squid proxy allowlist permits only: cdn.company.com, api.internal.company.com, assets.company.com, *.amazonaws.com on port 443. Additionally, the SRI integrity attribute on the script tag ensures that even if the cdn parameter is attacker-controlled, the browser will refuse to execute any script whose hash doesn't match sha384-oqVuAfXRKap7fdgcCY5uykM6+R9GqQ8K/uxy9rx7HNQlGYl1kPzQho1wx4JwY8w. The combination of VPC network isolation (blocking IMDS and arbitrary egress) plus SRI (blocking XSS via CDN parameter injection) closes both the SSRF and the client-side attack vectors.
